lesson.text: Remember? A story has characters (who), a setting (where and when) and a plot (what happens). Today: old stories called fables and folk tales, and the lessons they teach.
A fable is a short story, often with talking animals, that teaches a lesson, called its message. Read this one: The Beaver and the Heron.
All autumn, Beaver worked on her dam, stick by stick. Heron stood in the river on one leg and laughed. "Why work so hard? The river is gentle and the fish are fat." Beaver just said, "Rivers change."
Then winter came with a great storm. The river rose and roared. It flooded the reeds where Heron slept and swept her fish away. But behind Beaver's dam, the pond stayed calm and still.
Cold and wet, Heron came to the dam, and Beaver let her rest on the lodge until spring. "Next autumn," said Heron, "I will help you build." The message: get ready for hard times while times are easy.

A folk tale is an old story passed on by people telling it. In Stone Soup, a hungry traveller came to a village with only a pot and a stone. "I'll make stone soup," she said, "but it needs one carrot."

One neighbour brought a carrot, another an onion, another some beans, until the whole village had added something. They all shared a delicious soup. The message: when everyone shares a little, there is plenty for all.

To retell a story, say who is in it. Then say what happens at the beginning, the middle and the end, in your own words. Try it in the world: retell Stone Soup to a friend. Next: characters and their feelings.

exercises.prompt: In the fable, who worked hard all autumn?
exercises.hint: Look at the first sentence of the fable.
exercises.explain: "All autumn, Beaver worked on her dam."

exercises.prompt: What did Heron do while Beaver worked?
exercises.hint: Find Heron in the first part of the fable.
choices: stood on one leg and laughed
exercises.explain: "Heron stood in the river on one leg and laughed."

exercises.prompt: In the fable, the storm washed Beaver's dam away.
exercises.hint: What happened behind Beaver's dam?
exercises.explain: False: behind Beaver's dam, the pond stayed calm and still.

exercises.prompt: What is a fable?
exercises.hint: Think of the Beaver and the Heron.
choices: a short story that teaches a lesson
exercises.explain: A fable is a short story, often with talking animals, that teaches a lesson.

exercises.prompt: In Stone Soup, what did the traveller bring?
exercises.hint: Look at how the folk tale begins.
exercises.explain: She came with only a pot and a stone.

exercises.prompt: Retell the fable: put the events in order.
exercises.hint: What happens first, in the autumn?
exercises.explain: Beaver builds, Heron laughs, the storm comes, and Heron shelters at the dam.

exercises.prompt: How do you know the storm was strong?
exercises.hint: Find the words that describe the storm.
exercises.explain: The fable says the river "rose and roared": that shows a strong storm.

exercises.prompt: What is the message of Stone Soup?
exercises.hint: What happened when everyone added something?
choices: When everyone shares, there is plenty
exercises.explain: Each person gave a little, and there was enough soup for all.

exercises.prompt: Why did Heron offer to help next autumn?
exercises.hint: What happened to Heron because she did not get ready?
choices: She learned that getting ready matters
exercises.explain: The storm showed Heron why Beaver worked: getting ready for hard times matters.

exercises.prompt: A folk tale is an old story passed on by people telling it.
exercises.hint: Think of Stone Soup.
exercises.explain: True: folk tales were told and retold for many years before anyone wrote them down.

exercises.prompt: What did the villagers do in Stone Soup?
exercises.hint: Look at what each neighbour brought.
choices: Each one added a little food
They ate all the soup alone
exercises.explain: A carrot, an onion, some beans: each villager added a little.

exercises.prompt: What is the message of The Beaver and the Heron?
exercises.hint: What did Beaver do that Heron did not?
choices: Get ready for hard times while times are easy
exercises.explain: Beaver got ready in the easy autumn, so she was safe in the winter storm.

exercises.prompt: An ant could not carry a big crumb, so she called her sisters, and together they carried it home. What is the message?
exercises.hint: What changed when the sisters came?
choices: Working together makes hard jobs easier
exercises.explain: Alone the job was too hard; together it was easy.

exercises.prompt: Which detail shows that Beaver was kind?
exercises.hint: Kindness is how you treat others.
choices: She let Heron rest on her lodge
exercises.explain: Beaver let Heron rest until spring, even though Heron had laughed at her.

exercises.prompt: Fox boasted he was best at everything. When the river flooded, he could not swim, and little Otter pulled him out. What might Fox learn?
exercises.hint: Who helped Fox, and why could Otter do it?
choices: Everyone is good at different things
exercises.explain: Otter could swim when Fox could not: everyone has their own strengths.

exercises.prompt: Retell Stone Soup: put the events in order.
exercises.hint: How does the folk tale begin?
items: A traveller arrives with a pot
exercises.explain: The traveller arrives, asks for a carrot, everyone adds food, and they share the soup.

exercises.prompt: Match each story to its message.
exercises.hint: What did each story teach?
exercises.explain: Beaver got ready for the storm; the villagers shared their food.

exercises.prompt: Which story is each thing from?
items: a dam holds back a flood
exercises.hint: One story has animals and a river; the other has a hungry traveller.
exercises.explain: The dam and the flooded reeds are in The Beaver and the Heron; the pot, the stone and the shared food are in Stone Soup.

exercises.prompt: Sort the events: the beginning, middle or end of the fable?
items: Heron offers to help next year.
exercises.hint: Beginning: who they are and what they do. Middle: the problem. End: how it turns out.
exercises.explain: Beginning: Beaver builds and Heron laughs. Middle: the storm floods the river. End: Heron rests on the lodge and offers to help next year.

exercises.prompt: Match each story to the lesson it teaches.
items: Fox and Otter in the flood
exercises.hint: Think about what each main character learns or shows.
exercises.explain: Beaver got ready for hard times. In Stone Soup, sharing gave plenty. The ants worked together to carry the crumb. Otter saved Fox: everyone has their own strengths.
